_comment: Authorship and citation metadata for the Zenodo deposit, in Zenodo's own
standard file so it is edited here rather than inside a workflow script.
IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST DEPOSIT FAILED WITHOUT IT. Zenodo requires
metadata.creators and refuses to publish without it; 523 MB uploaded
successfully and the publish call returned HTTP 400. A deposit that uploads
and cannot publish looks like a network problem and is a metadata one.
Add `orcid` and `affiliation` to a creator when they are known — both are
optional to Zenodo and both make the record more useful to cite. Anyone who
should be credited on a future edition is added here, not in the script.
WRITE `orcid` AS THE FULL RESOLVER URL, https://orcid.org/0000-.... CITATION.cff
wants it in that form and Zenodo's API wants the bare identifier, so one must be
derived from the other; the bare one is derived, because that needs no URL
written into code, and a URL belongs here rather than there.
`deposit_excludes` names release assets that are NOT deposited to Zenodo. The
DOI should resolve to the data, and tiles are a rendering of the data —
regenerable from the GeoPackage with `rewt viewer-data`, and 312 MB of the 523
that v0.1.0-alpha archived. They stay a GitHub release asset because pages.yml
fetches them from there to serve the map; it is the deposit they leave, not the
release.
`concept_recid` ANCHORS THE VERSION CHAIN, and it exists because the first two
releases did not share one. The script created a fresh deposition per release, so
v0.1.0-alpha and v0.1.1-alpha became two unrelated datasets with two concept DOIs
(…22238250 and …22248272) rather than two versions of one. The badge and the
citation both named the first, which will now never resolve to the newest edition.
Both DOIs are permanent and cannot be merged. The live lineage is 22248272, from
v0.1.1-alpha onward; …22238250 is a superseded single-version concept. Every later
release is created with `actions/newversion` on the latest version of the recid
below, so there is one chain and it is declared rather than rediscovered.
